subject: Performance SLO & customer-led load test coordination (FinanceCorp)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jae Park <jae.park@financecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO & customer-led load test coordination (FinanceCorp)

Hi Jae 
- great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from today's discovery focused on performance/SLOs and a customer-led load test: 

Summary from call:
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 250 ms for standard text generation; p50 <= 100 ms.
- Throughput target: sustained ~100 req/s for the primary inference endpoint.
- Concurrency: expected peak concurrency ~200 simultaneous requests (burst up to 300).
- Streaming: must support chunked streaming for long responses; we validated that Redwood streaming will keep connection open and deliver tokens as generated.

Customer-led load test details we need from you to coordinate:
1) Preferred test window (timezone): suggested weekend windows are best to avoid production traffic.
2) IP allowlist: list of source IPs that you'll run tests from (we'll add to firewall).
3) Auth: will you use the test API key we provision or client credentials?
4) Test scripts: you mentioned k6 (preferred) but we can also accept Locust scripts. Please share the script or allow us to provide a starter k6 script we maintain.

What we will provide before the test:
- A dedicated test pool reserved for your run (to avoid noisy neighbor effects).
- Test account and API key provisioning instructions (we'll send API key via secure channel).
- A pre-test checklist and sample k6 script tuned to your scenario.
- IP allowlist guidance and support for opening network ranges.

Next steps / ask of FinanceCorp:
- Reply with your preferred 2 windows (include timezone) and the list of source IPs.
- Confirm whether you'll run k6 or Locust and share the test script if available.

I'll attach the starter k6 script and the provisioning doc in a follow up. Marissa & Neha 
looping you in for capacity reservation and infra readiness.

Thanks 
Logan

--
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Jae Park <jae.park@financecorp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Liu <david.liu@financecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & customer-led load test coordination (FinanceCorp)

Thanks Logan, really useful recap. A few quick answers and questions from our side:

- Preferred windows (PST):
  1) Sat 2026-03-14 02:00-06:00 PST (overnight)
  2) Sun 2026-03-15 22:00-02:00 PST (overnight)

- We'll run k6. We'll start with a baseline script (ramp-up to 100 req/s, hold 30m) and then a concurrency burst test to exercise 200-300 concurrent connections.

- IPs: we plan to run from our load agents in AWS us-west-2. I'll confirm exact IP ranges by tomorrow but expect a small set of elastic IPs.

- Auth: please provision a test API key tied to a test account. We prefer not to exchange keys over email; if possible, share via a secure channel (1Password or DocuSign/secure portal).

Questions:
1) Can Redwood support streaming tests in k6 that hold open connections and validate streamed token latency?
2) Any recommended headers or request patterns we should use to mimic production (e.g., session affinity, streaming-framing)?

We'll attach our initial k6 script once we confirm IPs.

Best,
Jae

--
Jae Park
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
FinanceCorp
jae.park@financecorp.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jae Park <jae.park@financecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-11T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & customer-led load test coordination (FinanceCorp)

Thanks Jae 
- good plan. Answers inline below and attached the starter materials.

1) Test windows: both proposed windows look good. We'll tentatively reserve Sat 2026-03-14 02:00-06:00 PST. Please confirm and we'll lock capacity.

2) Streaming in k6: k6 supports HTTP/1.1 long-polling but has limited native streaming semantics for chunked transfer. We've used a small helper harness that opens a streaming connection and measures first-byte latency and token arrival intervals. I attached a sample k6 script (k6-financecorp-loadtest.js) with a streaming helper and assertions for first-byte latency < 100ms and subsequent token pacing. If you prefer, we can run the streaming portion from our side and feed you telemetry.

3) Headers / request patterns: use Authorization: Bearer <test-api-key>, X-Client-Id: financecorp-loadtest, and accept: text/event-stream (if you plan to use SSE/streaming). For session affinity, include a custom header X-Session-Id to mimic sticky clients 
- we'll route by that header when requested.

4) Auth & keys: we'll provision a test API key and notify you via 1Password. Do not paste keys in email.

5) IP allowlist format: please provide CSV of IP ranges (example: 52.44.33.12/32). We'll add to firewall and confirm.

Attachments included: 
- k6-financecorp-loadtest.js (starter k6 script, includes streaming helper and assertion checks)
- redwood-test-account-instructions.pdf (how to consume test API key via 1Password + usage limits)
- financecorp-ip-allowlist.csv (template for you to fill with IPs)

Marissa / Neha: can you confirm we can reserve a capacity pool for Sat 3/14 02:00-06:00 PST? If not, we should propose the alternate slot. Also mark that streaming tests will require slightly different orchestration (long-lived connections).

Thanks 
Logan

--
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Pool size: equivalent of 8 inference workers (to validate sustained 100 req/s with headroom for bursts to 300).
- Streaming behavior: networking team flagged that long-lived streaming connections will need higher connection limits; we've increased per-worker file descriptor limits for the test.

Pre-test ops checklist (internal):

- Apply IP allowlist entries to staging firewall by Fri 2026-03-13 18:00 PST
- Route X-Session-Id header to dedicated pool for session affinity
- Enable enhanced metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, network stats) and a live dashboard link

Neha

Marissa
